response.summary: Three claims are supported. Data Center revenue is growing strongly year over year ($89.0 billion, up 117%, in the second quarter of fiscal 2027). Revenue is concentrated in a few direct customers. Export controls are restricting China revenue: a $4.5 billion H20 charge, and only about $60 million of licensed H20 revenue. Two claims have mixed evidence. Gross margin rose to 75.0% from 72.4% year over year, but it was flat sequentially and fell for fiscal 2026 as a whole. Supplier dependence is a named risk, partly offset by added redundancy. For an overweight, growth is confirmed, while customer concentration and China remain open risks and the margin trend is unclear.
next_steps: Quantify how much of customer concentration risk rests on the top direct customers and what purchase commitments they have disclosed.
Track sequential gross margin guidance for the next quarter to test whether expansion continues beyond the recovery from the H20 charge.
Check for any H200 China license progress and its potential revenue effect.
Review the supplier redundancy disclosures to judge how much the concentration risk has actually fallen.
